- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.3) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast lows by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects; cap subsequent forecast increases at +3% from peak.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model often holds or overshoots; adjust downward by 1–3% on day 4–6.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; shift forecast horizon 1–2 days earlier if sentiment shifts sharply.
- If model forecast is >75% of true outcome’s range, it’s likely overconfident; apply a 5–10% downward bias to high-end forecasts.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend after 10–15 days, model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% after day 10.
